episodes.title: Designing The Marble Machine's Programming System
episodes.description:
Wintergatan Update Summer 2026

    Parental Leave, July 20 to August 21, 2026 - I'm going to be home with my daughter on parental leave from July 20 to August 21. Back working on the Marble Machine August 24.

    Team Vacation and Summer Content Pause - My Team members are on vacation during the same period, July 20 to August 21, so there will be a pause in content over the upcoming month.

    Content Schedule - When we're back from vacation, we won't publish every Wednesday. The video deadlines are halting the Marble Machine rather than aiding it. Letting the design process dictate what needs to be done, and publishing videos whenever they're naturally ready, will optimize for Machine progress instead.

    Online Messages - In general, i do not read or reply to online comments and messages. The sheer amount of input makes it impossible to handle in the time available. It feels bad knowing that people put their hearts into messages without getting a reply, but I would never want a team or bots to write fake answers in my place. Thank you to everyone who has written heartwarming direct messages and comments on Wintergatan's online channels.

    Positive Perspective on Marble Machine Progress - I've solved all my real question marks about how this machine should look, feel and function. The tinkering research from the last few years has been a slow process, but in the end, very fruitful. All the work requiring inspiration is completed and in art that's actually the hard part. To make progress from here we only need hard work, discipline and elbow grease, easy peasy :)

    Negative Perspective on Marble Machine Progress - I think progress is too slow. I get stuck in details instead of executing the bigger unlocks. I'm spending too much time on the public-facing part of the project, managing all the administrative overhead that never shows in YouTube videos. Since becoming a father, I've reduced my work from 200% to only 100%, which means I have to be doubly deliberate with my focus. The build-in-public process is a double-edged sword, the joy of sharing the journey is mixed with distractions pulling me away from the necessary deep work. Over the years I've tried many times to re-shift my focus away from internet, now it's time to try again. I will spend my parental leave reflecting on this, building momentum towards that one decision, to take The Road Not Taken.

Thank you all and see you after the summer! //Martin

The Road Not Taken By Robert Frost

Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both
And be one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could

To where it bent in the undergrowth;
Then took the other, as just as fair,
And having perhaps the better claim,
Because it was grassy and wanted wear;

Though as for that the passing there
Had worn them really about the same,
And both that morning equally lay
In leaves no step had trodden black.

Oh, I kept the first for another day!
Yet knowing how way leads on to way,
I doubted if I should ever come back.
I shall be telling this with a sigh

Somewhere ages and ages hence:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.

episodes.title: Marble Machine Programming Wheel Design Challenge
episodes.description:
MARBLE MACHINE DESIGN CHALLENGE

Make the ultimate Snap-In Programming profile for the Marble Machine!
Send your Design ideas as Onshape links here:
https://forms.gle/SzoCR1bzwDiLcxkaA

Try Onshape Free - Engineers Get Up to 6 Months Pro with the Wintergatan Link:
https://onshape.pro/Wintergatan

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:
•⁠  ⁠Curved Stainless steel sheet metal base, 1mm thin, 1600mm diameter bend
•⁠  ⁠Holes are laser or watercut in the curved base

•⁠  ⁠Profiles Max Width 9mm
•⁠  ⁠Profiles Max Height above base 40mm
•⁠  ⁠Profiles lengths varies from 80mm-200mm
•⁠  ⁠3D Printed, design for printability

•⁠  ⁠Snaps in and out from the top surface (no fastening from the undersideof the base)
•⁠  ⁠Must stay perpendicular to base within +-1mm of top of profile
•⁠  ⁠Top reading surface can have different heights (20/30/40mm) within the same profile
•⁠  ⁠Center-center distance 10mm between programming channels
•⁠  ⁠Lengthwise position tolerance +- 0.4mm
•⁠  ⁠Heightwise position tolerance +-1mm

•⁠  ⁠Design submission must be Onshape Links, no further documentation

episodes.title: Can Marbles Play Drums Like a Human?
episodes.description:
The real story here is that I am finally making decisions, writing functional requirements and killing darlings. There are many snare sounds that I have decided that the machine should not be able to play side stick, rimshot, brushes etc. 
Narrowing down the functionality and sticking to a short list is progress IMHO :)
Next up: doing the same for all the instruments, defining what the output of the machine should be. Should have done it three years ago but wasn't in a place where I could make decisions then, better late than never I guess! :)

Good luck with everything you are doing! /Martin

Wintergatan Wednesdays and Livestream schedule 

Monday - LIVE 9:30-12:00 & 14:00-17:00
Tuesday - LIVE 9:30-12:00 & 14:00-17:00
Wednesday - VIDEO 16:00 (10 minute Weekly Progress Recap)
Thursday - LIVE 9:30-12:00 & 14:00-17:00
Friday - Easter Holidays

All times Stockholm CET Timezone.

These streams are designed to let Martin spend as much time as possible building the Marble Machine, while still bringing you along for the process. Come hang out with us in the workshop as it happens.

As always, times may shift slightly depending on the build, but this is the structure we’re aiming for going forward.

See you in the workshop and on Wintergatan Wednesday’s!

Alfons
